description: A plugin's own script runs only inside a sandboxed frame with no network, no cookies, no storage and no access to the app around it. It talks to its own plugin through a small bridge that reaches only the routes the plugin declared. The overlay surface is live: one transparent layer under every popover that is clipped to a few declared rectangles and never covers the terminal.
examples: A pixel pet walks across the screen while a session runs; it cannot read the terminal or call the network.
how_to: Install a plugin that declares a view and turn it on with third-party plugins enabled.
Its overlay view appears; clicks outside its declared rectangles go to the app underneath.
Turn the plugin or the master switch off and the frame is removed.
name: Plugin custom views
summary: a third-party plugin can draw its own page in a locked box, such as a pet that walks across the screen, without touching the app.
where: Anywhere on screen for an overlay view, under popovers and above the page, outside the terminal grid.
